title: Observability Ingest v2 Status Response
description: Response for GET /api/v2/observability/ingests/{ingest_id} (14-observability-ingest-v2 §3.2). Returns the manifest state plus one record per event. Polling is authoritative; a webhook is optional. Reusing the same ingest_id returns the persisted manifest, so a client that times out without a response treats the outcome as UNKNOWN and reads status by ingest_id rather than minting a replacement.
x-privacy-note: Ingest-manifest metadata only — client-minted opaque ids (ingest_id / event_id), an immutable SHA-256 payload DIGEST (never the payload), integer attempt counts, closed-enum states and dispositions, and terminal_reason strings drawn from a fixed, pre-written, server-side table. No user-authored or LLM-generated content, no PII, and no server internals reach this body, so it is safe to export to logs, telemetry and support tooling in full. Classified manifest_safe rather than aggregate_safe because nothing here is an aggregated statistic: it is per-event manifest metadata about the caller's own submission. Any future field that could carry user-controlled values (e.g. echoing a submitted name) MUST be annotated x-content:true with its own x-privacy-classification and MUST NOT inherit this one.

events_detail_available.description: True when per-event records back `events[]` (the receipts/outbox rows are still live); false when they have been age-purged and `events` is reported empty rather than guessed (14-observability-ingest-v2.md §5.2: full receipts/ledger are retained 7 days, then dropped, while the manifest's own retention window is not yet ratified and the 30-day claim rows carry no per-event state to reconstruct from). Lets a client distinguish 'this ingest genuinely has zero events' (never happens in practice) from 'the per-event detail behind this ingest has aged out' -- both would otherwise look like an empty `events` array.

allOf.description: When per-event detail IS available, events[] cannot be reported empty (every admitted event has exactly one receipt at admission time, §3.1) -- only the purged/unavailable case may report zero events.

CONVERSE guard: when per-event detail is NOT available (the receipts/outbox rows behind it have age-purged, §5.2), events[] MUST be reported empty -- a non-empty events array under events_detail_available:false would be fabricated per-event detail the server has just declared it no longer holds.

ManifestState.description: Request-level rollup derived from the per-event states. ADMITTED is the durable-queue acceptance point (the only state that returned 202). COMPLETED = every event reached a materialized/duplicate terminal; PARTIALLY_DEAD_LETTERED / DEAD_LETTERED = some / all events dead-lettered. NOTE: the design specifies the per-event admission state machine (§3.1) but does not enumerate an aggregate manifest vocabulary; this rollup set is a minimal faithful choice (see PR summary open question).

EventState.description: SDK-facing per-event status (§3.2). MATERIALIZED / DUPLICATE / DEAD_LETTERED are terminal; PENDING_VERSION is awaiting its per-emitter predecessor.

ReservationDisposition.description: Charge-on-persist lifecycle (§3.3, ratified). Reserved at ADMITTED, CONSUMED only in the materialization commit, RELEASED for every terminal dead-letter record.

ReplayOwner.description: Who owns replay/repair of a terminal event: tenant for malformed customer content, platform for infrastructure repair. Null until the event is terminal.

attempted_count.description: Number of delivery/materialization attempts recorded for this event.

terminal_reason.description: Sanitized, client-safe reason for a terminal outcome (no server internals). Null for non-terminal states.

terminal_code.description: Stable terminal reason code (subset of the v2 error taxonomy) for DEAD_LETTERED / PENDING_VERSION events; null otherwise.

then.description: Every terminal record (MATERIALIZED / DUPLICATE / DEAD_LETTERED) carries the immutable event hash (globally required), attempted count, capacity/quota disposition (globally required), a sanitized terminal_reason, and a replay_owner. The reason/owner keys must be present; they may be null where inapplicable (e.g. terminal_reason and replay_owner are null for a clean MATERIALIZED record). See §3.2.
A terminal dead-letter record must carry a NON-NULL sanitized reason and a concrete replay owner.
